items.title: Frankfurt Book Fair 2026: Germany Finds in Favor of Copyright Holders Against AI
items.excerpt: A regional court in Munich has twice ruled that LLMs are memorizing work, an illegal act of reproduction
items.rationale: A court decision: a Munich regional court has ruled that LLM memorization of works is illegal reproduction. This shifts the legal ground under every licensing and training-data dispute publishers are in.

items.title: Frankfurt Book Fair: Storytel’s Talks AI-translated Audiobooks
items.excerpt: The company has automated its translation publishing workflow and introduced Genie, a new AI-powered companion.
items.rationale: A major audiobook platform has fully automated its translation-to-audio workflow and launched Genie, an AI companion. This is a concrete production change, not a debate.

items.title: Intellectual Property Office registers UK’s first ‘human-authored’ certification mark
items.excerpt: The Intellectual Property Office (IPO) has registered the UK’s first certification mark for human-authored books.
items.rationale: Follow-up with a new official act: the UK IPO has formally registered a 'human-authored' certification mark, so the label now has legal standing instead of being only an industry stamp.

items.title: Barrierefreies Lesen und KI-gestützte Hörbuchproduktion
items.excerpt: Der Digital Publishing Award 2026 zeichnet Avneesh Singh, die Nahdet Misr Group, Pozotron Studio und ReadBee aus. Die Preisträger wurden am 7. Oktober auf der Frankfurter Buchmesse aus 42 Einreichungen ausgewählt.
items.rationale: Follow-up with a new result: the Digital Publishing Award winners are announced, including an AI-assisted audiobook production studio (Pozotron), showing which AI publishing tools the industry is endorsing.

items.title: ‘We have fine dining, and we have McDonalds’: Publishers hotly debate AI narration at FBF
items.excerpt: Publishers from Blinkist, Storytel and Horbuch Hamburg Verlag debated the value of AI narration on a panel, chaired by Chris Kling, CEO of Audio, at Frankfurt Book Fair today (7th October), with questions of distrust, value and listener preference raised.
items.rationale: Audio publishers at Frankfurt take a two-tier position on AI narration ('fine dining vs McDonalds'), which tells authors and producers where human narration is still expected to win.

https://www.thebookseller.com/news/intel.new_action: UK Intellectual Property Office formally registered the first 'human-authored' certification mark (an official registration decision, not covered by the 10/08 WIRED piece on the stamp).

https://www.boersenblatt.net/news/barrie.new_action: Digital Publishing Award 2026 winners announced on 7 Oct at Frankfurt (10/02 card covered only the 12 finalists).
